reminder.notes:
Reminder edits replicate over your Wi-Fi too

F62 phase E. The previous release put alarm actions on the local network; this
one puts the reminders themselves there.

### Features

- Add, edit or delete a reminder on one phone and the other picks it up and
  re-arms its alarms straight away, with no sign-in, no internet and no server
  involved -- only that both phones are on the same Wi-Fi. This works even on a
  device that cannot keep its sign-in session, which the cloud path depends on.
- Incoming changes go through the same merge the cloud sync already uses, so two
  phones editing at once settle exactly as they always have.
- Every mirrored action now records which path delivered it, over Wi-Fi or
  through the cloud, so a problem can be traced without guesswork.

### Bug fixes

- An edit made on one phone could take a long time to reach the other, or not
  arrive at all, whenever the cloud path was unavailable or the sign-in session
  could not be restored. The local path does not depend on either.
- A batch of changes too large to send in one piece is now left to the cloud
  sync instead of being split up, and is not marked as sent until it has
  actually gone out, so nothing is dropped quietly.

cards.notes:
Cards 2.5.0 — Background update checks, and no more double-downloading updates

### Features
- Cards now checks for updates periodically in the background (about every 6 hours) and posts a notification when one is found, in addition to the existing manual "Check for Updates" in Settings. Tapping the notification opens the app; the download and install still happen from the Settings sheet.

### Bug fixes
- The update downloader now persists its in-flight DownloadManager id and re-attaches to a still-running download instead of deleting the partial file and starting over — fixes re-downloading the same update from zero after backgrounding or reopening the app mid-update.
- The update sheet now re-syncs its progress on resume instead of occasionally showing a frozen progress bar.

localsender.notes:
Local Sender 1.0.11 - security hardening (full audit)

A full security audit (see AUDIT.md and THREAT_MODEL.md in the repo) and fixes for
every CRITICAL and HIGH finding it turned up. All local content is now encrypted
at rest, the macOS build is sandboxed again, and Drive backup no longer stores its
own key next to the data it protects.

### Features
- Google Drive backup is now sealed with a passphrase you set and never upload —
  Drive alone can no longer read a backup, only you can.
- A warning dialog when a device presents a different identity key than the one
  already trusted under that name, instead of an ordinary pairing prompt.

### Bug fixes
- Chat history, rooms, trusted-peer keys, peer profiles, network profiles, and
  device name are now encrypted at rest (previously plaintext in local storage).
- Fixed a path-traversal bug where an incoming file offer's name could write
  outside the downloads folder.
- Fixed an unbounded network frame length that let any device on the LAN push
  memory usage toward the app's limit with a single unauthenticated connection.
- A silent, unresponsive peer during pairing could lock the app out of pairing
  with anyone else; pairing now times out and recovers.
- A connection dropped mid-file-transfer no longer leaves a frozen progress row
  or an orphaned partial file on disk.
- Re-enabled the macOS App Sandbox (previously off since v1.0.1 to work around a
  Keychain hang); the underlying hang is now handled by an existing timeout and
  fallback, so sandboxing no longer breaks pairing.
- The identity key's on-disk fallback file (used only when the OS secure store is
  unavailable) is now encrypted instead of holding the raw key.

bchat.notes:
BChat 0.1.0-beta.1 — first beta

Text chat over a Bluetooth mesh. No internet, no SIM, no server, no account.
Nearby phones relay for each other, so someone out of direct Bluetooth range is
still reachable through the devices in between.

This is an early beta: expect rough edges, and expect to reinstall as the wire
protocol changes.

### Features
- 1:1 private chat, encrypted with Noise XX (mutual authentication, forward secrecy)
- Public Nearby room that every device in range can read; every message is signed
- Multi-hop relay with TTL bounds, duplicate suppression and message fragmentation
- Nearby peer list showing direct versus relayed peers and hop distance
- Message requests: a first message from a stranger waits for Accept or Block
- Delivery and read receipts, with the hop count shown on delivered messages
- Sender outbox: a message to someone out of range keeps retrying for 24 hours
- Rotating on-air identifiers, so a passive listener cannot track a device over time
- Safety-number verification per contact
- Background mesh service with a pause switch and four power modes
- Encrypted local message database

### Bug fixes
- None. First release.

### Not in this build
- Groups, photos, voice notes and file transfer
- The Wi-Fi LAN transport
- iOS

### Known limits
- Multi-hop relay is verified in simulation and on an emulator, not yet across three
  physical phones.
- Battery use in the higher power modes has not been measured on real hardware.
